_comment: Phase 1 matrix vs REAL repo. Recon (T0/T2) confirmed real prefixes are /api/techscape/v1/* and /api/travel/v1/* (NOT /api/techscape/* — the router mount adds /v1). 'admin' column below is the spec's branch-admin tier, which core/deps.py stores as role='manager' (bare 'admin' is reserved for the legacy top rank == super_admin — see core/deps.py docstring). Token minting REQUIRES --biz <active business id> AND --sub <real ts_users id whose actual DB role matches the column> — core/deps.get_current_user re-reads the DB row and ignores the token's role claim, so access_matrix.py's mint() must be given real per-role user ids via the GOGAGA_SUB_* env vars. (Historical note: mint() once passed no --sub/--biz at all; that was fixed in commit acdf499 during Phase 1, and this comment previously still described the broken behaviour as current.) Wiki uses 201/204 on create/delete; users/branches use 201 on create.
_notes: leads.py's assigned-only scoping (Phase 2 T1) is DONE — agent-tier GET/list is restricted to assigned_agent=self, manager+ stays business-wide. Status-code matrix above still shows 200/200/200/403 for GET (all non-viewer roles get 200; the ROW-LEVEL filtering isn't a status-code difference) — row-level proof needs real per-agent fixtures with different assignments, done in PHASE2_REPORT.md T1/T7 evidence, not this static spec.

calls.py (Phase 2 T7) mirrors the same pattern via lead_id join: agent-tier GET /calls/live returns only calls whose lead is assigned to them (still 200, filtered result). GET /calls/{id}/transcript and the WS /ws/calls/{call_id} live feed depend on a specific call's scope (in/out of the caller's assignment) — not expressible as a static per-role code here, verified via real fixtures in PHASE2_REPORT.md instead.

PATCH/DELETE target-id tests, out-of-branch 404s, role-elevation 403s, and the token-invalidation chain were verified in T3-T5 (Phase 1) and T1/T7 (Phase 2) task chains with real per-role DB fixtures (not this static spec) — see PHASE1_REPORT.md / PHASE2_REPORT.md.
logout is tested separately from the table above in practice (each call invalidates that role's own token) — run it last per role, not interleaved with the other rows.

webhooks_voice.py's POST /webhook/{provider}/voice and WS /webhook/{provider}/stream are NOT in this matrix — they use Plivo-signature auth, not JWT/roles, so a per-role expectation table doesn't apply. See PHASE2_REPORT.md for their verification (HMAC signature logic + simulated frame sequences).

ai-config (Phase 3 T2, added this sprint 2026-08-07): GET is require_role('viewer') so every authenticated role passes; PUT/seed are require_role('manager') so only admin(=manager)/super_admin pass. GET/seed auto-create a default config row on first access, so PUT is safe to re-run across sweeps (idempotent update, not insert). takeover.py's /calls/{id}/takeover/* and /calls/{id}/events ARE now in this matrix (Phase 3 T10), using the all-zeros UUID as a deliberately nonexistent call. That covers the two outcomes that ARE static: viewer is rejected at require_role('agent') with 403 before any lookup, and agent+ get a clean 404 from the scope check rather than a 500. The state-dependent outcomes — 200 on a real active call, 409 on a non-active one, and the assigned-vs-unassigned 404 split for agent-tier — still need real fixtures and a live call, so they are NOT asserted here.

PHASE 4 ROWS (added 2026-08-08) — real prefixes read off routers/travel/__init__.py, not guessed: packages mounts at /packages, whatsapp at /whatsapp, follow-ups at /follow-ups, activity at /activity-log, usage at /analytics; payments and reports declare their own FULL paths and mount with NO prefix, which is why /payment-links and /report-schedules sit directly under /api/travel/v1. Role gates were read off each router's require_role(): packages read=viewer / write=manager; payment-links read=viewer / write(create,transition)=agent; whatsapp outbox=viewer, send=agent; reports+report-schedules read=viewer, run-due/send-whatsapp/create/patch/delete=manager; follow-ups list+rules-read+PATCH=agent, rules-write+schedule=manager; activity-log=manager; analytics/*=manager.

PHASE 4 id-dependent routes follow the takeover precedent: the all-zeros UUID asserts the two STATIC outcomes only — rejected at require_role before any lookup (403), or a clean scope miss (404). Anything state-dependent is deliberately absent: the 200 on a real row, the 409 on an illegal payment transition, the 501 on /reports/{id}/pdf?format=pdf, and the agent-tier assigned-vs-unassigned 404 split on follow-ups all need real fixtures, not a static table. Note the asymmetry between GET /packages/{id} (404 for ALL FOUR roles — read is viewer, so viewer clears the gate and gets the same scope miss) and PATCH/DELETE /packages/{id} (403 for agent AND viewer — write is manager). That asymmetry is the point of listing both.

PHASE 4 probe bodies are chosen so a sweep cannot spend money or send a message. POST /payment-links pins gateway:'stub' — get_gateway('stub') always returns the deterministic StubGateway, so the row minted is a stub:// link even in an environment where RAZORPAY_KEY_ID is configured; leaving gateway unset would let the factory pick razorpay and mint a REAL link. POST /whatsapp/send deliberately passes an invalid recipient: normalize_msisdn() is the first statement of every provider's send_template(), so agent+ get a 422 before any provider I/O and nothing is ever transmitted — that 422 is asserting the role gate passed, not the send working. POST /report-schedules pins is_active:false so the created probe row is never picked up by the scheduler. PUT /follow-ups/rules re-asserts the day-1 rung with DEFAULT_LADDER's own values (nudge/whatsapp), so the upsert is a semantic no-op rather than a config change. POST /reports/scheduled/run-due keeps dry_run=true (its default) — reports are built and rendered, nothing is delivered and last_run_at is not stamped.

POST /webhook/razorpay is NOT in this matrix and must not be added — it is authenticated by the gateway's X-Razorpay-Signature HMAC, not by a JWT or a role, exactly like webhooks_voice.py's Plivo routes above. A per-role expectation table does not apply to a route no role can hold. Its verification is signature-based instead (correct sig accepted / tampered body / tampered signature / missing header / wrong secret all rejected) — see PHASE4_REPORT.md T2. Unlike the Plivo verifier it fails CLOSED when no secret is configured (DEBT-12), so on an unconfigured environment it answers 403 to every caller including a valid one.

PHASE 4 rows NOT yet executed against a live database: this file is the spec, and the cross-phase sweep it feeds still needs Supabase (B-P4-06, inheriting B-SPRINT2B-01). Every Phase 4 route WAS confirmed to reject unauthenticated callers with 401, which proves the auth gate is present and correctly ordered but says nothing about per-role codes — role resolution re-reads ts_users from the DB.

SCOPE BUG FOUND WHILE WRITING THESE ROWS (not fixed here — followups.py was outside the authoring task's file ownership): POST /follow-ups/schedule passes body.lead_id straight to FollowUpService.schedule_for_lead, which SELECTs travel_leads.business_id and then never compares it to the caller's. A manager can therefore schedule follow_ups rows against another tenant's lead_id; the inserted rows carry the caller's business_id and the victim's lead_id. That is why the row above expects 201 for manager+ on the all-zeros lead — a nonexistent lead returns [] and still answers 201. Once the ownership check lands, the expected code for a nonexistent/out-of-scope lead becomes 404 and this row must be updated with it.

GET /calls/{id}/events had an authorization bypass until Phase 3 T10: it called get_call_scoped() but discarded the result, and get_call_scoped RETURNS None rather than raising. Any agent-tier user could read any call's event log, including cross-tenant, since get_events() filters on call_id alone. The 404 rows above are the regression test for that fix.
